summary: A modal panel anchored to an edge. Modal behaviour — focus trap, Escape, scrim — with the shape of a side panel.
useWhen: work that is long or list-shaped: filters, a record's detail, a run of settings
the page behind should stay visible as context while a task is done beside it
a form long enough that a centred dialog would scroll its own actions off screen

useInstead.when: the user is making a decision, especially a destructive one
useInstead.why: a modal is centred and small enough that the thing being confirmed cannot be scrolled past

useInstead.when: the panel should stay open while the user works elsewhere
useInstead.why: a drawer traps focus and marks the rest of the page inert. A panel that does not do those things is layout, not an overlay

useInstead.when: the content is a short menu of actions

start.use: navigation and hierarchy, which readers expect at the leading edge

end.use: the default — detail and editing beside the record that opened it

top.use: rare: a global search or command surface

bottom.use: touch-first layouts, where the bottom edge is the reachable one

sm.use: a short form or a filter list

lg.use: a record detail with its own sections

title.note: required — it is the dialog's accessible name

footer.note: pinned to the bottom edge, so actions stay reachable in a long panel

requires: `title`, which becomes the dialog's accessible name via aria-labelledby
notes: start and end follow writing direction, so a right-hand drawer in English is a left-hand one in Arabic with no second variant
renders nothing when closed and portals when open: a closed overlay left in the tree is still keyboard-focusable
only the body scrolls, so the title stays on screen — the one piece of context a user needs while working down a long list

antiPatterns.dont: a Drawer that stays open while the user edits the page behind it
antiPatterns.why: it traps focus and marks the rest inert; a keyboard user cannot reach the page behind it
an edge panel is tall, so the confirm button can sit below the fold — the one control that must never be missed
